issues.desc: checklist.json CHK-001 (lines 4-19) declares the design-record integrity/digest outcome but its files.test array is empty. No concrete verification command or artifact check is named for the source SHA-256, payload-prefix, or Sections 1-27.6 preservation claim, so this item is not independently verifiable from the INIT checklist.

checklist.json CHK-011 (line 289) requires FI-1 through FI-5, Section 19 thresholds, and Section 20 mutation rows, but its only relatedDocs entry is the experience-layer ablation plan; neither background.md nor the checklist links the approved source plan/record that defines those identifiers. A fresh implementer cannot locate the exact threshold and fault-injection contract from this story metadata.

checklist.json CHK-012 uses P50s, LPT, and dist reader/writer without expanding them, while background.md does not define those terms. A fresh reviewer can infer scheduling intent but not the exact resource and ordering contract.

The INIT background is dominated by implementation invariants and the triggering request; it does not clearly name the primary user/operator problem (for example, costly full validation versus the need for safe, auditable reuse) or the concrete benefit users should receive. Add a concise user-value statement and identify the beneficiary roles so the implementation can be judged against product impact, not only soundness mechanics.

CHK-001 through CHK-013 provide strong component-level userSees statements, but the story has no single end-to-end acceptance outcome showing how an operator recognizes the complete program is usable: choose a mode, receive an auditable execute/reuse/escalate disposition, preserve full-authority boundaries, and reach a safe rollback/closure state. Add an integrated completion scenario or explicit final user-visible outcome to prevent the plan from finishing as disconnected subsystems.
